- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85.00), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk — add 2–5% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00), model lags in correction — adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early bearish momentum — apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment drops below 0.30 in last 5 days.
- If multiple auction events occur in 7–10 days, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast growth by 1–2% per event unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
